Prune Multipart USDM Rings in Pure NumPy and Persist a 395 MiB Cube Instead of GeoParquet

Unlike Hurricane Winds—where the core decision was selecting HURRECON over CLIMADA—your Drought workflow already has a locked acquisition baseline of 1,357 weekly U.S. Drought Monitor (USDM) polygon archives (2000–2025) plus 3 early-2026 recovery buffers. The critical engineering task for the coding agent is pruning continental U.S. (CONUS) polygon rings at the binary `.shp` part level before calling ArcPy, compiling the 26-year series into a single in-memory `(1360, 267, 1140)` `uint8` cube (`drought_weekly_cube.npz`) and a compact PR-only geodatabase feature class (`pr_weekly_polygons`), and generating the verified 1–3–5 hazard raster.

395 MiB

Exact RAM footprint of the complete 1,360 × 267 × 1,140 uint8 spatiotemporal state cube (~4 MB on disk via np.savez_compressed, reloading in <0.2 s).

Part-Ring Binary Prune

Because national `_M` shapefiles merge CONUS, Hawaii, and PR into 1–5 multipart rows, prune individual polygon rings (`parts` offsets) via zero-copy `np.frombuffer` before invoking ArcPy—skipping ~60–65% of weeks entirely and stripping 100,000+ CONUS vertices on active weeks.

Why Skip GeoParquet

Unclipped multipart CONUS bounding boxes defeat GeoParquet row-group pushdown, `PolygonToRaster` requires Esri features, and adding `pyarrow`/`geopandas` violates `AGENTS.md`. A single PR-clipped GDB feature class (~20 MB) + `.npz` cube is faster and 100% native.

Frozen Tertile Primary Rank

Classify primary indicator WD1 = ND1 / 26 into Low : 1, Medium : 3, High : 5 using frozen island-wide tertiles (q33.3, q66.7), paired with fixed 3 & 7 wk/yr planning breaks for sensitivity.

Why Zero-Copy Part-Ring Pruning + a Compressed Cube Beats Both Naive ArcPy Loops and GeoParquet

Your acquisition pipeline (drought.py) has already verified and cached 1,357 baseline weekly ZIPs (2000-01-04 to 2025-12-30) and 3 early-2026 recovery buffer ZIPs (2026-01-06 to 2026-01-20) in output/drought/cache (~1.53 GB compressed). Each weekly `_M` shapefile contains only 1 to 5 dissolved rows (`DM = 0..4`, except for 225 pre-2013 archives with up to 76 rows), where a single `DM` row is a massive multipart polygon spanning the continental U.S., Alaska, Hawaii, and Puerto Rico.

This multipart geometry structure has two major engineering consequences for your agent:

  • Record-level bounding boxes and unclipped GeoParquet fail to prune CONUS: When a single multipart `DM` row covers both Hawaii (-155°W, 19°N) and Maine (-67°W, 47°N), its record-level bounding box overlaps Puerto Rico's longitude (-67.9°W to -65.2°W) and nearly touches its latitude (17.9°N to 18.5°N). Converting unclipped national ZIPs to GeoParquet still pays the full 1,360-ZIP extraction cost upfront, fails to prune multipart CONUS rows via row-group bbox pushdown, introduces non-standard `pyarrow`/`geopandas` dependencies outside `arcgispro-py3`, and still requires converting geometries back into Esri feature classes for `arcpy.conversion.PolygonToRaster`.
  • Zero-copy binary part-ring pruning in pure NumPy solves both I/O and ArcPy geometry overhead: Inside `utils/drought/usdm_archive.py`, the agent already reads raw `.shp` bytes in memory from each cached `.zip`. By slicing each record's point buffer with `np.frombuffer(shape_bytes, dtype='<f8')` and indexing by the shapefile's `parts` offset array, the agent can discard every CONUS/Hawaii/Alaska ring in <10 ms per ZIP (~12–15 seconds total across all 1,360 archives!). Weeks with zero rings intersecting Puerto Rico (~850+ weeks) skip ArcPy entirely, and the remaining ~500 active weeks pass only the 2 to 5 tiny Puerto Rico rings (<500 vertices instead of 150,000+ CONUS vertices) into ArcPy!
Mandatory Binary Part-Ring Pruning Algorithm (utils/drought/usdm_rasterize.py):
1. For each record in the `.shp` byte stream (offset rec_off, content start p = rec_off + 8, shape_type == 5):
  • Read num_parts, num_points = struct.unpack_from('<ii', shp_bytes, p + 36).
  • Slice part indices: parts = np.frombuffer(shp_bytes, dtype='<i4', count=num_parts, offset=p + 44).
  • Slice vertex coordinates: pts = np.frombuffer(shp_bytes, dtype='<f8', count=2 * num_points, offset=p + 44 + 4 * num_parts).reshape(-1, 2).
2. Transform the Puerto Rico bounding envelope [-68.15, 17.80, -65.10, 18.60] into the archive's source CRS (no-op when WGS84; project envelope once when Albers).
3. For each ring slice ring = pts[start:end] (where start = parts[k], end = parts[k+1] or num_points): keep ring if and only if its bounding box intersects the PR envelope.
4. Fast short-circuit: If zero rings across all records intersect the PR envelope → set all assessed land cells (mask == 1) to 0 (None) and exterior/unassessed cells to 255 in the uint8 cube without calling ArcPy!
5. Active-week fast path: Construct an in-memory feature class from the kept PR-only rings, project to EPSG:32161 (WGS_1984_(ITRF00)_To_NAD_1983), run RepairGeometry and Dissolve(DM), append the clean PR polygons to drought_prepare.gdb/pr_weekly_polygons (with MAP_DATE, ROLE, DM, and X_CODE = DM + 1), and call PolygonToRaster(CELL_CENTER) snapped to reference250.tif to populate slice t of the (1360, 267, 1140) uint8 cube. Save the finished cube to output/drought/data/drought_weekly_cube.npz.

Agent Implementation Contract for the Six USDM Structural and Spatial Edge Cases

Your November 12, 2026 inspection in docs/drought_processing_plan.md uncovered six dataset-specific gotchas across the 1,360 archives and 654,160 reference statistic rows. Because there are no competing drought models to choose between, the quality of your course deliverable depends entirely on how deterministically your code handles these six edge cases. The implementation agent must enforce every rule in the table below.

Discovered Anomaly / Requirement Empirical Evidence in Frozen Snapshot Mandatory Agent Implementation Rule Verification Assertion in validation_report.json
1. Raw DM=0 vs. Drought-Free None USDM shapefiles encode DM ∈ {0, 1, 2, 3, 4} for D0–D4 (UNL Classification) and omit polygons for None. Map X = int(DM) + 1 so D0: 1, D1: 2, D2: 3, D3: 4, D4: 5. Assign None: 0 to assessed land cells outside D0–D4 polygons, and 255 to unassessed/ocean cells. Assert set(np.unique(cube)).issubset({0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 255}) and confirm 2000-01-04 has 100% of assessed land cells equal to 0.
2. Multi-Feature Same-Class Archives 225 weekly ZIPs (2000–2012) contain multiple rows per DM value (up to 76 features on 2012-10-16), logged as MULTIPLE_DM_FEATURES. After part-ring pruning to the PR envelope and projecting to EPSG:32161, run arcpy.management.RepairGeometry and arcpy.management.Dissolve grouped by DM before area checks or rasterization. Assert post-dissolve feature count is at most 5 per week (`DM 0–4`) and cross-class polygon intersection area is 0.0 m².
3. Culebra & State API Reference Disagreements 6 reference statistic warnings: on 2015-08-04 and 2015-08-11, Culebra (72049) API reports both None: 100% and D2: 100% (200% sum). Derive all spatial cell states strictly from the verified USDM polygons (which place Culebra in D2 on both dates). Never use API None percentages as a spatial fill rule. Confirm Culebra control point (-65.3034, 18.3133) evaluates to X = 3 (D2) on 2015-08-04 and 2015-08-11 while preserving the API warning flag.
4. Island-by-Date Assessed Domain (Mona Coverage) Mona (-67.90, 18.08) had no polygons in the 2026 sample but lies inside D0 polygons in 2015 archives. Empty clips alone do not prove an island was assessed. Build an island-by-year intersection ledger across all 1,357 weeks for mainland, Vieques, Culebra, and Mona. Where an island's assessment continuity is verified across the cohort, fill non-polygon weeks as None: 0; otherwise flag as 255. Record per-island valid week counts N_VALID (1,357 expected) and report whether Mona is included or masked as NoData in the primary vs. sensitivity raster.
5. Source CRS Heterogeneity Sample .prj files declare WGS84 (EPSG:4326) despite older UNL GIS metadata citing Albers Equal Area. Inspect each archive's actual .prj WKT at runtime via arcpy.SpatialReference; transform the PR pruning bbox when .prj is projected (e.g., Albers) and apply WGS_1984_(ITRF00)_To_NAD_1983 when projecting to EPSG:32161. Log distinct source CRS WKT hashes across all 1,360 weeks and assert 100% of rasterized outputs match EPSG:32161, cell size 250.0 m, and extent 1,140 × 267.
6. Recovery Buffer Isolation Cohort includes 1,357 baseline weeks (2000–2025) plus 3 early-2026 END_BUFFER weeks; pre-2000 START_BUFFER weeks do not exist. Mask the cube by ROLE == 'BASELINE' (1,357 slices) for all occupancy sums (N_D1, W_D1, F_D1, DSCI_cell). Use the 3 END_BUFFER slices only to test whether late-2025 drought events terminate. Assert occupancy denominator is exactly 1,357 weeks (26.0 years) and zero 2026 buffer weeks enter W_D1 or F_D1.

Vectorized Indicator Math, Orographic Physical Context, and the Leeper Event State Machine

Across Puerto Rico, persistent northeast trade winds rise over the Cordillera Central and Sierra de Luquillo, producing abundant orographic rainfall on the northern windward slopes while casting a sharp rain shadow across the southern coastal plain (Ponce, Salinas, Guayama, Coamo, Lajas) and eastern offshore islands (Herrera & Ault, 2017; PR DRNA, 2016). During strong El Niño and Saharan Air Layer episodes—most notably the historic 2014–2016 drought (Mote, Ramseyer, & Miller, 2017)—moisture suppression expands from the southern rain shadow into the eastern and central water-supply watersheds (Carraízo / Loíza and La Plata reservoirs).

Primary & Supporting Vectorized NumPy Formulas

Given the baseline state subarray X_base of shape (1357, 267, 1140) (`uint8`), define the validity indicator V = (X_base <= 5). A cell c is eligible for final ranking if and only if N_VALID(c) = V.sum(axis=0) == 1357. Over all eligible cells, compute in vectorized `float64`:

ND1(c) = ∑t=1..1357 1[ 2 ≤ X(c,t) ≤ 5 ]
WD1(c) = ND1(c) / 26.0   [weeks/year in D1–D4]
FD1(c) = 100.0 · ND1(c) / 1357.0   [% of baseline weeks]
WD2(c) = (∑t=1..1357 1[ 3 ≤ X(c,t) ≤ 5 ]) / 26.0   [weeks/year in D2–D4]
DSCIcell(c) = (100.0 / 1357.0) · ∑t=1..1357 X(c,t)   [0 to 500 scale]

Notice the clean algebraic identity for cell-level UNL DSCI: because a single cell on date t occupies 100% of one exact category X(c,t) ∈ {0..5}, the weighted exact-category sum 1·pD0 + 2·pD1 + ... + 5·pD4 simplifies to 100 · X(c,t). Thus the temporal mean DSCI_cell(c) is simply 100 × the mean encoded severity X̄(c).

Leeper et al. (2022) 3-Week Recovery State Machine

To separate chronic multi-month droughts (like the 80+ week 2014–2016 event) from brief dry spells without counting every week as a new event, Leeper et al. (2022) define a drought event as initiating when a cell reaches D1 or worse (X ≥ 2) and terminating only after three consecutive weeks of D0 or None (X ≤ 1). Short 1- or 2-week dips to D0/None remain part of the active event.

Censoring & Buffer Rules:
• Left-Censored: If X(c, t0) ≥ 2 on 2000-01-04 (or if an event initiates within the first 3 weeks after a D0 state on 2000-01-04), flag LEFT_CENSORED = 1.
• Right-Censored vs. Buffer-Resolved: Evaluate termination of events active on 2025-12-30 using the 3 END_BUFFER weeks (2026-01-06, 2026-01-13, 2026-01-20). If X ≤ 1 across all 3 buffer weeks, the event cleanly terminates at the end of 2025; otherwise flag RIGHT_CENSORED = 1.

Step-by-Step Implementation Guide for the Coding Agent

To preserve the clean repository structure defined in AGENTS.md and README.md, the agent must not create sprawling new folders, introduce `pyarrow`/`geopandas` GeoParquet dependencies, or leave intermediate weekly rasters behind. All new logic belongs inside utils/drought/, exposed through drought.py and wired cleanly into the existing geoprocessing contract.

  1. Add utils/drought/usdm_rasterize.py (Binary Part-Ring Pruner, GDB Feature Appender & Cube Engine): Consume download_validation.json (which links to download_manifest.json) and output/shared/grid/grid_spec.json. Verify that download_validation.json["passed"] == True. If output/drought/data/drought_weekly_cube.npz already exists and its recorded manifest SHA-256 matches, reload the `(1360, 267, 1140)` `uint8` cube in <0.2 s. Otherwise, loop through the 1,360 verified archive entries in manifest["gis"]: apply the zero-copy NumPy `.shp` part-ring vertex filter (`parts` array offsets + `np.frombuffer(shp_bytes, dtype='<f8')`) against the PR bounding envelope (`[-68.15, 17.80, -65.10, 18.60]`). For the ~850+ weeks with zero intersecting rings, set assessed land cells directly to 0 (None) and exterior cells to 255. For the ~500 active weeks, build `arcpy.Polygon` features from the kept PR-only rings in `memory/`, project to `EPSG:32161` (`WGS_1984_(ITRF00)_To_NAD_1983`), run `RepairGeometry` and `Dissolve(DM)`, append the dissolved PR polygons into `drought_prepare.gdb/pr_weekly_polygons` (~15–25 MB total across all 26 years), rasterize via `PolygonToRaster(CELL_CENTER)` snapped to `reference250.tif`, and save the completed `(1360, 267, 1140)` `uint8` cube to `drought_weekly_cube.npz` (~4 MB compressed).
  2. Run the Three Built-In Spatial QA Benchmarks Before Ranking:
    • State & Municipio Area Reconciliation: Recompute weekly cumulative D0–D4 area percentages and reconstructed DSCI from the 250 m cube and compare against drought_acquisition.gdb/statistics, confirming that the 2015-08-04 and 2015-08-11 Culebra (72049) anomalies are resolved in favor of the D2 polygon geometry.
    • Boundary-Week Cell-Assignment Sensitivity (Syllabus Section 3): Using the persisted `drought_prepare.gdb/pr_weekly_polygons` feature class on the six pilot dates (2000-01-04, 2012-10-16, 2015-08-04, 2015-08-11, 2026-01-06, 2026-08-04), compare CELL_CENTER against MAXIMUM_COMBINED_AREA (with precautionary tie-breaking toward the higher DM class) and record the exact cell agreement percentage in the validation JSON.
    • 2014–2016 Historical Drought Footprint Verification: Extract peak severity and cumulative D1+ / D2+ weeks during the 2014–2016 drought cohort and verify high-exposure alignment across southeastern/eastern Puerto Rico, Carraízo/La Plata watersheds, Vieques, and Culebra (PR DRNA, 2016; Herrera & Ault, 2017).
  3. Compute Continuous Indicators, Freeze Breakpoints, and Write Drought_rank250.tif: Slice the 1,357 BASELINE weeks to compute W_D1, F_D1, W_D2, and DSCI_cell, and run the Leeper et al. (2022) 3-week recovery state machine across all 1,360 weeks (using the 3 END_BUFFER weeks strictly to resolve right-censoring). Compute and freeze (b1, b2) under Scheme A, evaluate Schemes B and C, record the land-area class-transition matrix (`km²` and `%` changed), and write the aligned integer raster Drought_rank250.tif (values strictly in {1, 3, 5}, exterior/unassessed : NoData) to output/drought/data.
  4. Extend Verification & Combined Map Integration: Add offline unit tests in tests/test_contracts.py for (a) the binary `.shp` multipart ring pruner (verifying that CONUS rings are stripped while PR rings are kept), (b) the 0..5 / 255 byte encoding, (c) the Leeper 3-week recovery state machine, and (d) quantile breakpoint freezing. Verify that "HurricaneWinds_rank250" + "Drought_rank250" in ArcGIS Pro Raster Calculator produces Combined_sum250.tif with exact scores {2, 4, 6, 8, 10} and strict NoData propagation across all four islands.
